tiers.name: Ensuite, with a view of Skiddaw

events.line: A fell-running club has booked every room and will eat everything, twice.
It has rained for three days, nobody can face the fells, and your guests are on their fourth pot of tea.
Walkers from three countries, all asking whether the lake is always that colour.
A pipe burst in the night. The plumber is on his way and wants a lot of tea and some of your time.
Snow has closed the pass. Two guests stayed on. Nobody else could get in.
A breakfast inspector tried your black pudding, nodded gravely and left a form.

upgrades.name: Two more rooms in the loft
upgrades.text: More beds and more breakfasts, and a longer list of things that can go wrong on a Sunday night.

upgrades.name: Evening meals for the house
upgrades.text: Walkers off the fell will pay for a hot dinner. They will also tell you how it compares.

upgrades.name: A place in the walking guides
upgrades.text: Your name in the books people carry up hills.

asks.title: A drenched party
asks.text: Eight walkers have come down off the fell at {deed} wetter than anyone should be, asking, in the voice of the damp, whether there is a drying room.

options.label: Open the boiler room and put the kettle on
options.say: Steam, tea and grateful strangers. One of them leaves a review that mentions the biscuits.

options.label: Offer the airing cupboard for a small fee
options.say: They pay, they dry and nobody is quite as grateful as they might be.

options.label: Say you are full, which is true on a technicality
options.say: They squelch off up the road. Word of that gets about too.
